story: On Control (1986), Janet Jackson and producers Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis set funk and disco rhythms in synthesizers and a rap sensibility. In Virginia Beach in 1991, Pharrell Williams and Chad Hugo, entering a talent contest against their friends Missy Elliott and Timbaland & Magoo, were found by producer Teddy Riley. Timbaland, born in Norfolk and schooled in Virginia Beach, went to New York with Elliott when DeVante Swing of Jodeci signed her group Sista. He took hip-hop's drum breaks into R&B, using breakbeats to break up a track's smooth flow. In 1996 he produced most of Aaliyah's One in a Million and Ginuwine's first album, and in 1997 all of Elliott's Supa Dupa Fly. Rodney Jerkins (Darkchild), raised in New Jersey, produced Brandy and Monica's "The Boy Is Mine" in 1998 and Destiny's Child's "Say My Name" in 1999. The Neptunes produced all of Kelis's first album, Kaleidoscope, in 1999 and in 2001 had their first worldwide hit, Britney Spears's "I'm a Slave 4 U". In Britain, bootleg garage remixes, one of them of "The Boy Is Mine", fed the rise of UK garage. In 2004 all 12 Billboard Hot 100 number ones were by African-American artists.

disagreements: No Wikipedia article for 'Y2K R&B' as a genre; the story is built from Contemporary R&B, Timbaland, The Neptunes and Rodney Jerkins articles.

Start date: our record says 1998; Timbaland's breakthrough productions (Aaliyah's One in a Million, Ginuwine's debut) are 1996 and Supa Dupa Fly 1997 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timbaland?action=raw). The Contemporary R&B article says 'in the second half of the 1990s, [[The Neptunes]] and Timbaland set influential precedence'.

Origin: our record says Virginia Beach. The Neptunes formed there and Timbaland went to school there, but Timbaland was born in Norfolk, Missy Elliott in Portsmouth, their Swing Mob work was in New York, and Rodney Jerkins (Darkchild) is from New Jersey.
notes: Home language English. The Timbaland article calls his style 'stuttering', matching our record's sound line; no source used describes the era as 'Y2K R&B'. The 'after' beat rests on UK garage bootlegs and the 2004 Hot 100; nothing found on where the style ended around 2006.
